jobs.description:
Overview & Responsibilities

Background

Under the framework of its Multi-Year Rule of Law for Stability Programme, and with financial support from the Government of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, the International Development Law Organization (IDLO) will implement the Damal Programme Phase II (2026–2030) in Somalia and Somaliland. Building on the achievements, lessons learned, and institutional partnerships established under the first phase of the Damal Programme, Phase II seeks to strengthen social cohesion, improve public trust in justice and security institutions, and enhance equitable access to justice for vulnerable populations. The programme recognises that effective, accessible, and accountable justice systems are fundamental to peaceful societies, conflict prevention, inclusive governance, and sustainable development. By strengthening both formal and community-based justice mechanisms and promoting collaboration among justice and security institutions, the programme aims to contribute to a more responsive, inclusive, and resilient justice sector.

Damal II will be implemented primarily in underserved, rural, urban, and conflict-affected areas where justice gaps, insecurity, and social exclusion remain significant barriers to peace and development. The programme adopts an integrated approach that combines Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR), reconciliation, justice-security coordination, legal aid, referral mechanisms, community engagement, institutional capacity development, research, and evidence-based programming. It also places particular emphasis on strengthening access to justice for women, girls, internally displaced persons (IDPs), minority clans, persons with disabilities, youth, and other vulnerable justice seekers who continue to face disproportionate barriers in accessing fair and timely justice services. The programme is structured around three mutually reinforcing intermediate outcomes:

  • Intermediate Outcome 1: Vulnerable groups have improved access to gender-responsive ADR and reconciliation services.
  • Intermediate Outcome 2: Justice-security coordination mechanisms in urban and conflict-affected areas are more responsive, trusted, and effective.
  • Intermediate Outcome 3: Vulnerable justice seekers with cases beyond ADR mandates receive timely, coordinated, gender-responsive, and rights-based justice services through an integrated referral system.

To ensure a strong, evidence-based, and context-responsive start-up, the Damal Programme Phase II will commence with a preparatory phase, designed to refine implementation strategies, validate assumptions underpinning the Theory of Change, strengthen institutional coordination, and ensure interventions respond to evolving political, legal, security, and social dynamics.

A central feature of the above will be an extensive programme of stakeholder consultations across all programme target locations. As part of the consultations, IDLO will engage representatives from the justice sector, executive institutions, legislative bodies, the judiciary, prosecution services, law enforcement agencies, traditional dispute-resolution actors, civil society organisations, academia, women's organisations, youth representatives, community leaders, development partners, and local communities. These consultations will facilitate agreement on implementation priorities, coordination mechanisms, referral pathways, institutional roles, and approaches for strengthening access to justice within different geographic and institutional contexts.

The Assignment

Under the overall supervision of the IDLO Field Programme Manager, and in close collaboration with the Damal II Programme Team and IDLO technical teams, consortium partners, and relevant government counterparts, the Consultant shall design and undertake a comprehensive Baseline Assessment and Legal Analysis for the Damal Programme Phase II (2026–2030).

The assignment will provide the evidence required to establish a credible starting point for programme monitoring, validate key assumptions underpinning the Theory of Change and inform implementation decisions during the preparatory phase. It will build on, rather than duplicate, the evidence generated under Damal Phase I (2021-2026) and previous IDLO-supported ADR programming.

The assessment will cover the jurisdictions and prospective programme locations identified in the Damal II Project Document. The precise geographic coverage and sampling framework will be agreed during the preparatory stage, taking into account the phased programme approach, the status of location selection, security and access conditions, the availability of existing data and the level of institutional maturity in each jurisdiction.

Where final programme locations have not yet been confirmed, the assignment shall adopt a phased approach. Initial comparative analysis across prospective locations shall inform geographic targeting and site selection, while detailed baseline measurement shall focus on confirmed or formally shortlisted programme locations. The Consultant shall clearly document the geographic coverage and limitations of each baseline value and indicate where additional measurements may be required once final implementation locations are confirmed.

The assignment shall be organized around two interrelated workstreams. Please refer here for the details.

Methodology

The assessment shall adopt a mixed-methods, participatory, and evidence-based research approach, combining quantitative and qualitative data collection with legal and institutional analysis. The methodology shall integrate factual information, institutional evidence, stakeholder perceptions, and community experiences to provide a comprehensive understanding of the plural justice environment and establish a robust baseline for Damal Programme Phase II. The assessment should not only document the current status of justice institutions and services but also analyse the factors influencing access to justice, institutional performance, justice-security coordination, referral systems, and community trust across the programme's target areas.

The Consultant shall develop a comprehensive research framework that clearly links the Damal II indicators and thematic areas to the relevant research questions, data sources, collection methods, respondent groups and analytical approaches. The framework shall include an indicator-to-research-question and indicator-to-method matrix and shall specify how each programme indicator requiring baseline measurement will be assessed.

Separate sampling approaches shall be developed, as appropriate, for ADR users, community members, justice and security institutions, service providers, case and referral records, and other relevant stakeholder groups. For quantitative indicators, the Consultant shall provide the sampling frame, sample-size calculation, selection procedure and expected level of precision or confidence. Where probability-based sampling is not feasible, the Consultant shall justify the alternative approach and clearly explain the resulting limitations.

Data shall be disaggregated by sex, age, disability, displacement status and geographic location, where relevant to the indicator and safe to collect. The Consultant shall identify in advance the indicators and respondent groups for which each form of disaggregation will apply. Information on minority or clan affiliation shall be collected only where directly relevant, necessary and safe, through voluntary self-identification and with appropriate confidentiality and risk-mitigation measures.

Primary data collection shall focus on validating existing findings, updating baseline information, and generating new evidence in areas where information is limited or where significant contextual changes have occurred since the previous baseline assessment. Particular emphasis shall be placed on understanding justice needs, institutional performance, community perceptions, referral systems, justice-security coordination, and barriers affecting vulnerable justice seekers.

Primary data collection and review of existing records shall employ an appropriate combination of:

- Key Informant Interviews (KIIs);- Focus Group Discussions (FGDs);- Institutional assessments;

- Survey;- Community consultations;- Direct observation where appropriate;- Case studies of selected districts and justice pathways; and- All research instruments, interview guides, sampling approaches, and data collection tools shall be determined by the relevant research question and indicator. All research instruments, interview guides, questionnaires, sampling procedures and data-collection protocols shall be developed by the Consultant and approved by IDLO before field implementation. Instruments shall be piloted in an appropriate programme location and revised based on the results of the pilot. Where instruments are administered in Somali or other relevant languages, the Consultant shall ensure accurate translation and, where appropriate, back-translation or independent verification of key terminology and concepts.

Throughout the assignment, the consultant shall work closely with the Damal II Programme Team and with IDLO technical teams, consortium partners, and relevant government counterparts to ensure methodological rigour, technical quality, and alignment with programme objectives. Regular technical consultations will be held throughout the assignment to review progress, discuss emerging findings, and ensure that the assessment responds to evolving programme needs during the preparatory phase.

Given that the Baseline Assessment forms one of the principal analytical products of the Damal II preparatory phase, the research process will be highly consultative. Draft methodologies, preliminary findings, and draft reports will be reviewed by IDLO, consortium partners, and relevant government counterparts. National stakeholders will participate in validation workshops to verify findings, strengthen ownership, and ensure that the final assessment accurately reflects the realities, priorities, and perspectives of the justice sector and affected communities.

Key deliverables and Timeline

The consultancy will be undertaken during the Damal Programme Phase II preparatory period. The assignment is expected to be completed over approximately 6-8 weeks, with the exact commencement and completion dates to be agreed between IDLO and the selected consultant.

The consultant will work closely with the Damal II Programme Team throughout the assignment to ensure that findings continuously inform programme design, the Theory of Change validation process, and other preparatory activities. Deliverables will be reviewed and approved by IDLO before acceptance.

All research datasets, interview transcripts (translated into English where required), coding frameworks, legal review matrices, baseline indicator datasets, GIS or mapping products (where applicable), and other research materials generated during the assignment shall be submitted to IDLO as part of the final deliverables. These materials shall become the property of IDLO and will support future programme monitoring, learning, adaptive management, and subsequent analytical work during Damal II implementation.

Please refer here for the detailed deliverables and correspondent indicative timelines.

Job Requirements

IDLO seeks an experienced senior research and justice sector specialist with demonstrated expertise in conducting complex institutional assessments, legal analyses, and mixed-methods research within fragile and conflict-affected settings. The consultant should possess:

- An advanced university degree (master’s degree or higher) in Law, Justice Studies, Governance, Political Science, Public Administration, Development Studies, Peace and Conflict Studies, Social Sciences, or a related discipline.- At least 10 years of progressively responsible professional experience conducting justice sector assessments, legal and institutional analyses, governance research, political economy analysis, or rule of law programming in fragile or conflict-affected contexts.- Demonstrated expertise in plural justice systems, Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR), justice sector reform, legal aid, access to justice, justice-security coordination, governance, and institutional capacity development.- Strong knowledge of the legal, political, institutional, and socio-cultural context of Somaliland and/or Somalia, including experience working with government institutions, justice sector actors, civil society organisations, and development partners.- Proven experience designing and implementing qualitative and quantitative research methodologies, including legal reviews, institutional assessments, Key Informant Interviews (KIIs), Focus Group Discussions (FGDs), stakeholder mapping, and baseline studies.- Demonstrated ability to synthesise complex information into high-quality analytical reports and policy-oriented recommendations.- Excellent stakeholder engagement, facilitation, communication, and coordination skills, with experience working in multi-stakeholder and multidisciplinary environments.- Excellent written and spoken English. Knowledge of Somali will be considered a strong asset.

Terms & Conditions

The consultancy will primarily be home-based, with travel to programme implementation areas and stakeholder locations as required to undertake field research, institutional consultations, and validation workshops. The consultant is expected to undertake missions to selected programme locations, subject to prevailing security conditions and operational requirements.

The consultancy period, level of effort, remuneration, and payment schedule will be specified in the consultancy contract. Payments will be linked to the satisfactory completion and approval of agreed deliverables in accordance with IDLO's contractual procedures.

All work produced under this assignment, including reports, datasets, interview records, analytical tools, presentations, and supporting documentation, shall become the property of IDLO. The consultant shall maintain strict confidentiality regarding all information obtained during the assignment and comply with IDLO's policies on research ethics, data protection, safeguarding, and information security.

The work ranges from low-level engine integration to high-level questions about what a game can do once it has access to a live knowledge graph. The early phase is primarily exploration, but the destination is a production-ready SDK that other developers depend on and owning it through that transition is part of the role.

jobs.description:
O que buscamos

Buscamos um(a) Engenheiro(a) de Software GenAI Sênior para atuar no desenvolvimento de produtos baseados em Inteligência Artificial Generativa (LLMs) em ambiente de produção.

O profissional trabalhará em conjunto com o Arquiteto de Soluções GenAI, transformando definições arquiteturais em aplicações robustas, escaláveis e observáveis. Será responsável pela implementação de agentes de IA, pipelines RAG, APIs e soluções Full Stack, garantindo qualidade, performance e governança das aplicações de IA.

Responsabilidades

  • Desenvolver produtos baseados em LLMs para ambiente de produção;
  • Implementar pipelines RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation);
  • Desenvolver agentes inteligentes utilizando LangChain e LangGraph;
  • Construir chatbots, copilots e aplicações baseadas em IA Generativa;
  • Implementar orquestração multi-modelo utilizando LiteLLM;
  • Desenvolver soluções com Function Calling e gerenciamento de memória para agentes;
  • Desenvolver aplicações Backend em Python e aplicações Full Stack utilizando .NET (C#) e React/TypeScript;
  • Construir APIs REST robustas com processamento assíncrono (Streaming/Async);
  • Aplicar padrões de resiliência, como Circuit Breaker, Retry e Timeout;
  • Desenvolver testes automatizados, incluindo Evals para modelos LLM;
  • Implementar monitoramento e observabilidade de aplicações de IA, acompanhando consumo de tokens, latência, custos e desempenho;
  • Atuar na investigação e resolução de problemas em produção;
  • Participar de Code Reviews, ADRs, PoCs e documentação técnica;
  • Trabalhar em conjunto com Arquitetura, Produto e Engenharia na evolução das soluções.

Requisitos e Qualificações

Obrigatórios

  • Experiência mínima de 4 anos em desenvolvimento de software;
  • Pelo menos 1 ano de experiência prática com aplicações baseadas em LLMs em produção;
  • Experiência com:
    • LangChain;
    • LangGraph;
    • Implementação de RAG;
  • Domínio em Python;
  • Experiência com .NET (C#) e/ou React com TypeScript;
  • Desenvolvimento de APIs REST;
  • Mensageria e processamento assíncrono;
  • Conhecimento em sistemas distribuídos;
  • Experiência com Cloud (Azure, AWS ou GCP);
  • Docker;
  • Pipelines CI/CD;
  • Experiência utilizando pelo menos um dos provedores:
    • Azure OpenAI;
    • Amazon Bedrock;
    • Google Vertex AI / Gemini;
    • Anthropic Claude;
  • Experiência com Prompt Engineering;
  • Git;
  • Vivência em metodologias ágeis.

Diferenciais

  • LiteLLM;
  • Bancos vetoriais (Pinecone, pgVector, Azure AI Search);
  • CrewAI;
  • AutoGen;
  • Semantic Kernel;
  • MCP (Model Context Protocol);
  • LangSmith;
  • Arize AI;
  • RAGAS;
  • DeepEval;
  • Guardrails para IA;
  • Tratamento de PII;
  • Kubernetes;
  • Certificações Cloud;
  • Inglês avançado ou fluente para conversação.

Perfil Comportamental

Buscamos profissionais com:

  • Perfil analítico e investigativo;
  • Facilidade para resolver problemas complexos;
  • Senso de dono e responsabilidade sobre as entregas;
  • Boa comunicação e colaboração entre equipes;
  • Interesse constante por Inteligência Artificial e novas tecnologias;
  • Organização e atenção à qualidade do código;
  • Capacidade de atuar em ambientes dinâmicos e de rápida evolução;
  • Proatividade para propor melhorias técnicas e de arquitetura.

jobs.excerpt: At Bishop Fox, security isn't just a job - it's our passion.
jobs.description:
At Bishop Fox, security isn't just a job - it's our passion. As leaders in continuous offensive security and penetration testing, we deliver world-class customer experiences. Trusted by over a quarter of the Fortune 100, half of the Fortune 10, and top global media companies, we help safeguard digital landscapes. Our Cosmos platform, honored as Best Emerging Technology by SC Media, exemplifies our commitment to innovation.

Joining Bishop Fox means collaborating with a curious and dedicated team. You'll tackle complex challenges for some of the world's most recognized organizations, securing their networks against real-world threats. With nearly 20 years of industry contributions - including 16 open-source tools and 50 security advisories published in the past five years - we're committed to making the digital world safer.

Given our exceptional growth, we are expanding and hiring a Pen Tester to join us on this exciting journey. We’re looking for a talented, experienced professional hacker to help us secure some of the world’s most complex software and sophisticated technologies. You’ll be working alongside our US and internationally-based teams supporting clients across multiple industries.                         

                        

Who Are You and What You’ll Do

You’re a cybersecurity consultant with a strong offensive security mindset and a passion for understanding how modern applications, cloud platforms, APIs, and emerging technologies operate at a deep technical level. You enjoy uncovering security weaknesses, thinking creatively about attack paths, and helping organizations solve complex security challenges through practical, risk-focused assessments.

At Bishop Fox, you’ll work on a wide variety of security engagements including Cloud Security Assessments, Mobile Application Security Testing, Hybrid Application Assessments (HAA), and AI/LLM Security Assessments. You’ll evaluate modern applications and distributed systems across cloud-native, mobile, backend, and AI-enabled environments.

Your responsibilities will include performing hands-on security testing, analyzing application behavior, reviewing source code, identifying realistic exploitation scenarios, and validating security controls across modern architectures. You’ll work closely with clients and internal teams to deliver high-quality technical assessments and actionable remediation guidance.

As a consultant, you’ll contribute throughout the full engagement lifecycle from scoping and test planning to execution, reporting, and client presentations. Success in this role requires strong technical depth, structured testing methodologies, effective communication skills, and the ability to adapt quickly to new technologies and environments.

Your Experience

  • 4+ years of experience in application security assessments, penetration testing, or offensive security engagements
  • Strong understanding of application security fundamentals, modern attack techniques, and common vulnerabilities affecting web applications, APIs, mobile applications, and cloud-native environments
  • Hands-on experience testing REST APIs, including authentication/authorization flaws, IDORs, injection vulnerabilities, session management issues, and business logic flaws
  • Strength with AWS services and cloud security concepts, including IAM, STS, S3, Lambda, API Gateway, CloudTrail, CloudWatch, and secure communication patterns such as SigV4
  • Solid understanding of networking and web fundamentals, including HTTP/HTTPS, TCP/IP, DNS, API communication flows, cookies, headers, and related concepts
  • Experience reviewing source code for security issues in Java, C#, and Python applications
  • Knowledge of secure coding principles and common risks such as SSRF, insecure deserialization, injection vulnerabilities, sensitive data exposure, and insecure cloud integrations
  • Understanding of SDLC, CI/CD pipelines, and secure development practices
  • Experience using security assessment and code review tools such as Burp Suite, Semgrep, Git, AWS CLI, and API testing/debugging tools
  • Comfortable working across Linux, Windows, and macOS environments
  • Experience or strong interest in AI/LLM security, including prompt injection, RAG risks, insecure integrations, excessive permissions, and the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to deliver clear, actionable findings and communicate technical risks to both technical and executive stakeholders
  • Experience following structured testing methodologies, documentation standards, and validation/retesting workflows
  • Strong collaboration and interpersonal skills when working with security, engineering, and client teams
  • Ability to manage multiple concurrent engagements while maintaining high-quality deliverables and attention to detail
  • Curious, adaptable, and professional mindset with a passion for continuous learning and emerging security trends

Nice to Have

  • Exposure to hardware or embedded device security testing
  • Familiarity with cloud-native and serverless architectures
  • Consulting or client-facing experience
  • Relevant security certifications or hands-on research contributions

Why Bishop Fox

At Bishop Fox, we're driven by a simple mission: deliver exceptional quality to our clients, foster a vibrant and fulfilling environment for our team, and champion excellence within our industry. Our core values, which we live by every day, are:

  • Be Excellent to Each Other
  • Do the Right Thing
  • Do What You’ll Say You’ll Do
  • Get Better Together
  • Give a Sh*t

At Bishop Fox, we're committed to providing benefits that support your well-being and professional growth. Here's a glimpse of what we offer:

  • Generous Time Off and Company-Wide Holidays
  • Team Events and International Travel Opportunities
  • Work From Home Support
  • Training Budget

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, including sexual orientation and gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. jobs.description:
Overview

Clinical Pharmacist - VytlOne Specialty-Remote

VytlOne is currently seeking an experienced Clinical Pharmacist to join our growing Specialty Pharmacy in Lubbock, TX. This is an excellent opportunity for a Pharmacist to make a positive impact in the lives of the patients we care for, with a devoted pharmacy operations team.

Job Summary

The Clinical Pharmacist provides clinical pharmacy services for specialty pharmacy patients and internal teams in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, accreditation standards, policies, and procedures. This role reviews medication therapy for safety and appropriateness, supports prior authorization and utilization review activities, provides patient counseling and drug information, documents assessments and care plans, collaborates with providers and internal teams, and supports quality improvement, compliance, and operational initiatives. The Clinical Pharmacist may also dispense prescribed medications and oversee pharmacy technician activities as permitted by law and assigned by leadership.

Our Company

In July 2025, Maxor National Pharmacy Services became VytlOne — we are rewriting the rules to champion healthier healthcare communities. By uniquely combining PBM and Pharmacy Services into one integrated powerhouse, VytlOne doesn't just support our partners, we help them reach their full potential. Our new name reflects the important role we play in delivering innovative, mission-centric pharmacy solutions that unlock revenue, growth, and higher outcomes for our hospital, health system, health center, and employer partners. Pharmacy is a catalyst for our partners to achieve their goals.

For 100 years, VytlOne has created something that has set the stage for the next 100 to be Rxtraordinary! As the only truly integrated, independent PBM and pharmacy services partner, only we can help hospitals, health centers, and providers unlock millions of dollars of revenue..

Your Mission Is Our Mission

This campaign reflects our commitment to furthering and supporting our partners' mission by unlocking new streams of revenue and increasing cost savings, so that additional funds can be reinvested in their team, expanded access, and patient services.

One Team

Culture and people are the most critical ingredients to our success. It is your expertise and our unique WOW (Way of Working) that we want to maintain and nurture as we grow. We operate as one with our partners — an ally and advocate. Please join us on this journey as we turn toward the next 100 years while never forgetting where we started or how we made it here— it's going to be Rxciting

Our Locations

The VytlOne team brings robust experience, diverse perspectives and passion from a nationwide team of 1600+ professionals located in more than half of the US states.

Salary is $150K-$155K DOE and specialty certification

Responsibilities

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS (These duties must be performed with or without reasonable accommodation. This document in no way states or implies that these are the only duties to be performed by the employee occupying this position):

  • Interpret and fill drug orders accurately and timely
  • Ensures the appropriateness of all medication orders, new prescriptions or refills, in reference to the client’s diagnosis, weight/body surface area, allergies, and drug interactions as evidenced by a review of the active medication profile, provider notes, and available pertinent laboratory information.
  • Conduct/Review Drug Utilization Reviews to check for drug duplication, interactions or allergies.
  • Review non-formulary drug requests using predetermined criteria.
  • Review prior authorization requests using predetermined criteria.
  • Maintain current knowledge of drug therapies and drug reactions and interactions by reading professional literature, attending seminars and through professional affiliations.
  • Contact and confer with physicians regarding questions or irregularities with prescription practice whenever safety or established alternatives have not been utilized.
  • Monitor drug therapy for contraindications, interactions, allergies and appropriateness.
  • Documents / maintains initial patient assessments, reassessments and care management plans in the electronic patient management program, e.g., Asembia, CPR Plus.
  • Provide drug information to meet the needs of medical and nursing staff members through direct contact or in-service programs.
  • Provide patient information and counseling.
  • Participate as an active member and facilitator in process improvement teams.
  • Prepare provider newsletters or articles to keep providers updated. Provide individual and group training, in-services and other consultations to unit staff and providers to optimize therapy.
  • Work with medical directors and staff in developing and carrying out various clinical initiatives.
  • Generate and review standard monthly and quarterly reports, as required.
  • Attend and participate in other programs, committees, meetings, and functions as required.
  • Assist in the development of clinical, utilization management, ad hoc and production reports and programs.
  • Assist in formulary, rebate analyses and pharmacoeconomic studies and initiatives.
  • Perform retrospective drug utilization review: identify drug, physician, and patient utilization trends; make interventions as appropriate; monitor and document outcomes.
  • Assist in the generation, maintenance, and distribution of formulary alternative lists, maintenance drug lists, and new drug to market lists.
  • Work cooperatively with other staff members to enhance the team concept.
  • Supervise pharmacy technicians in the routine performance of their duties.
  • Participate in the development and implementation of the Performance Improvement Program.
  • Assist in overseeing clinical procedures.
  • Complete facility audits as assigned.
  • Maintain regular attendance in accordance with established policies and procedures.
  • Perform other job-related duties as assigned.
  • Promptly report any allegations of impropriety to the Compliance Department.
  • Comply with VytlOne’s Ethical Business Conduct policy and VytlOne’s Compliance Program.
  • Remain free from exclusion under the OIG and SAMS Medicare/Medicaid lists.
  • Complete required training, as assigned, within the established timeframes.

    • Qualifications

    Experience: Residency trainimg or 2 years post-graduate pharmacist experience in specialty pharmacy, ambulatory care, managed care, infusion, retail, hospital, or another clinically relevant pharmacy setting preferred. Experience conducting clinical review, patient counseling, medication therapy assessment, prior authorization support, care plan documentation, or interdisciplinary collaboration strongly preferred.

    Education: BS or Pharm. D. from an accredited school of pharmacy required. Current, unrestricted pharmacist license in the employee’s primary state of practice required, with ability to obtain and maintain additional state pharmacist licenses as business needs require.

    Licenses: May be required to obtain and maintain additional state pharmacist licenses, including non-resident licenses, based on patient location, pharmacy operations, payer requirements, or business needs.

    Certifications: Specialty pharmacy, immunization, medication therapy management, sterile compounding, or other role-related certifications may be preferred or required based on assigned duties, pharmacy services, and applicable regulatory requirements.

    Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

    • Knowledge of federal and state pharmacy laws, clinical pharmacy practice standards, specialty pharmacy workflows, medication safety principles, drug utilization review, prior authorization processes, patient counseling requirements, clinical documentation standards, and applicable accreditation, regulatory, and payer requirements.
    • Ability to evaluate medication therapy for appropriateness, safety, contraindications, interactions, duplications, adherence concerns, and other patient safety risks, and to communicate evidence-based recommendations clearly to providers, patients, caregivers, and internal teams.
    • Proficiency using pharmacy management systems, electronic patient management platforms, Microsoft Office applications, secure communication tools, and other technology required to support remote specialty pharmacy operations.
    • Ability to organize, prioritize, and manage clinical, operational, and documentation tasks to meet patient care, provider, payer, compliance, and business timelines.
    • Ability to use available clinical resources, policies, procedures, systems, and team support effectively to resolve patient, provider, payer, and operational needs.
    • Ability to communicate clearly, professionally, and compassionately with patients, caregivers, providers, pharmacy team members, payers, and other internal and external stakeholders, including when explaining clinical recommendations, documentation needs, coverage requirements, or sensitive patient information.
    • Ability to learn and use job-related software, pharmacy systems, electronic patient management platforms, secure communication tools, and reporting applications accurately and efficiently.
    • Ability to maintain accurate, timely, and complete clinical documentation, patient records, intervention notes, care plans, and required pharmacy records in accordance with company policy, documentation standards, and applicable regulatory, accreditation, and payer requirements.
    • Ability to evaluate clinical and operational workflows, identify opportunities for improvement, support policy and procedure implementation, and contribute to strategies that improve quality, compliance, patient care, and operational effectiveness.
    • Knowledge of quality improvement principles, performance improvement activities, audit readiness, outcome monitoring, and procedures used to support safe, compliant, and effective specialty pharmacy services.

At GSK, we have bold ambitions for patients, aiming to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade. Our approach to R&D

Position Summary

The Budget and Contracts Manager plays a key role in GSK meeting its upper quartile performance objectives. This role is responsible for managing the clinical site agreement and budget process for US Pharma / Vaccines studies. This position reports into the ICBP Associate Director (Investigator Contracts Benchmarking and Payments).

The Budget and Contracts Manager work with sites to obtain, confirm, and maintain required site level information that is necessary for the accuracy of clinical site agreements, and negotiate per patient budgets according to FMV parameters and following any exception processes.

Responsibilities

This role will provide YOU the opportunity to lead key activities to progress YOUR career. These responsibilities include some of the following:

  • Comprehensive knowledge of clinical development process and importance of meeting major study milestones.

  • Site contracting language and study budget benchmarking/fair market value analysis experience.

  • Demonstrated ability to effectively communicate (written and verbal) and influence key stakeholders at all levels of the organization and externally.

  • Ability to establish strong working relationships with internal and external stakeholders (e.g. legal, compliance, finance and sites).

  • Serves as main point of contact for internal and external stakeholders to meet site contracting/budgeting goals.

  • Liaise with GSK study team members to understand study specifics (enrollment goals, timelines, etc.) and provide study status reports including challenges and lessons learned.

  • Generates site-specific agreements using approved templates and any applicable study parameters.

  • Proposes site budgeting solutions to issues that may arise during development/negotiations of contract/budget cycle to enhance negotiation strategy and ensure deliverables are met.

  • Establishes strategies around investigator budget template development and/or budget negotiation parameters to reflect GSKs specifications, communications and required processes. Initiates and introduces creative ideas and solutions.

  • Works with study leads/SMEs to negotiate contract terms and conditions using fall back language and in collaboration with the US legal liaison, functional teams, and sites. Ensures agreements are clear, comprehensive, and complete.

  • Develops detailed investigator grant per patient budget estimates according to protocol specifications through currently available software package/resources/FMV tools.

  • Updates detailed investigator grant per patient budget estimates template according to protocol amendment specifications.

Why You?

Basic Qualification
We are seeking professionals with the following required skills and qualifications to help us achieve our goals:

  • 2+ years’ experience in clinical research and Bachelor’s degree, or 3+ years’ experience in clinical research and Associates degree (or equivalent) or 5+ years’ experience in clinical research without higher degree

  • Experience ensuring that clinical trial agreements are managed, and issues are appropriately escalated across the governance framework.

  • Experience with clinical study budget benchmarking and fair market value analysis, investigator site contracting, and investigator grant payments.

  • Experience with using Clinical Trial Management Systems (CTMS) and Trial Master Files (TMFs).

  • Experience participating in internal and external inspections and developing/implementing both preventive and corrective action plans.

Preferred Qualification

  • Familiar with AI tools/technology

  • Ability to create and maintain power queries and v-lookups is preferred

  • Experienced user of GrantPlan/GrantManager is preferred

  • Thrives in a matrix environment

  • Able to work independently, in a fast-paced environment

  • Has strategic thinking skills

  • Ability to analyze trend and metrics data (especially related to quality and performance) to communicate progress and drive continuous improvement.

  • Comprehensive knowledge of the clinical development process and protocol design.

  • Operationally focused with understanding of big picture strategy preferred.

  • Demonstrated ability to effectively communicate (written and verbal) and influence key stakeholders at all levels of the organization both internally and externally.

  • Able to manage multiple projects and priorities working across several trials and study teams.

  • Flexible and responsive to new ideas in a changing environment.

  • Recognizes potential obstacles or risks and works proactively to resolve them within set timelines. Escalates issues appropriately, articulating the actions required from members of the team.

#GSK-LI

About the role:

Gartner Analysts are industry thought leaders who create must-have insights, market predictions and best practices for a broad range of world-leading organizations. A Director serves as a leader within Gartner’s Business and Technology Insights (BTI) group. Utilizing research and analytical skills, a Director plays a significant role in producing pragmatic and provocative insights which Gartner clients consume and apply to propel their business toward key objectives. They are a trusted source of advice for clients, reinforcing Gartner’s value every day by engaging them via in-person meetings, virtual meetings, sales support visits and Gartner conferences to discuss complex client challenges and offer appropriate recommendations.

As part of Gartner’s Corporate Assurance Practice, you will join a dynamic team focused on advising General Counsel (GC) and other assurance leaders at the world’s largest companies to create greater value for their firms. This role will meaningfully expand insight and support for GCs. We are looking for an entrepreneurial, self-motivated, and ideas-driven individual to help serve clients on the topics below.

Career experience with the development and deployment of privacy and information governance process, specifically from the perspective of in-house legal departments, will be valuable, as will deep familiarity with specific privacy workflows – including privacy impact assessments, consent management, subject rights requests, etc.-- and collaboration with leaders in other corporate functions such as IT, Data & Analytics, Cybersecurity, etc.

The successful candidate will be comfortable discussing and researching topics including:

  • Legal’s role in establishing and maintaining a defensible privacy program

  • Information governance processes, challenges, workflows, and cross-functional relationships

  • Evolving privacy issues and how they impact organizational strategy, including sensitive personal information, privacy and AI, consumer trust, and data ethics

  • Emerging privacy regulations and issues (e.g., biometrics, AI governance, cross-border transfer restrictions)

What you will do:

  • Create innovative, thought provoking, and highly leveraged “must-have insights” content

  • Develop new insights and ideas through thought leadership and offer compelling, actionable approaches to client's needs and requests that accelerate the client's ability to act

  • Serve as a leading authority on privacy and information governance topics, such as:

    • Privacy strategy and program management,

    • GDPR, CCPA, and other leading privacy regulations,

    • Privacy impact assessments and DPIAs,

    • Cross-border data transfer restrictions and processes,

    • Data inventory and mapping,

    • Data subject rights requests processes,

    • Cookies and consent and preference management,

    • Evolving issues in the privacy landscape, including AI and privacy, biometrics, and consumer trust and preferences.

  • Stay abreast of external trends in the privacy landscape, including related areas like AI and AI governance.

  • Collaborate with peers and other experts across teams (e.g., Legal, IT, Finance) to understand client challenges, current market dynamics, evaluate vendors, and establish shared and consistent thought leadership and positions on relevant issues

  • Develop content and insight around emerging topics on AI governance

  • Develop in-depth analysis to identify the root cause of a client’s barriers or overall needs and reframe thinking to drive strategy forward

  • Demonstrate thought leadership in establishing Insights positions across a team of analysts

  • Bring provocative, independent insights to Gartner leaders that can evolve the course of a research agenda

  • Research, analyze and predict market trends and shifts to provide clients and vendors with actionable insights

  • Provide clients and prospects with actionable advice aligned to their designated content area via virtual or face-to-face interactions

  • Create and deliver high value presentation materials on and off stage for Gartner events, industry and professional association conferences, and client briefings

  • Support BTI and Sales: Provide sales support serving as voice of the market to help Insights teams create content and to drive engagement with clients to make progress against their critical priorities to grow their business

  • Provide high quality and timely content peer review

  • Build credibility as an industry expert to represent Gartner insights, methodology and strategy

  • Actively participate in innovation, ideation, and research discussions and collaborate effectively with peers in the Insights community

  • Identify research process improvements or develop new processes that help the team and BTI provide excellent service delivery

  • Be a mentor and a coach by supporting more junior team members

  • Be client-centric while actively seeking to help clients engage regularly and often with Gartner insights and interactions

What you will need:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience; JD degree preferred

  • 10+ years of relevant experience, including experience working in privacy, information governance, or within a corporate in-house legal department dealing with privacy and information governance

  • Demonstrated experience leading or coordinating privacy risk management efforts, setting or executing privacy strategy, working on information or data governance efforts across multiple stakeholder groups, and reviewing and synthesizing emerging privacy and related regulations

  • Demonstrate executive presence; with the ability to establish credibility with executives and additional stakeholders

  • Experience with AI governance highly desirable

  • Demonstrated executive presence; can immediately establish credibility with executives and additional stakeholders

  • Strong organizational skills; ability to work under tight deadlines and produce high quality deliverables

  • Demonstrate excellence in research and writing ability

  • Strong written and verbal proficiency, analytical and presentation skills; ability to engage clients and respond effectively to questions

  • Proficient in analyzing and synthesizing data; can effectively apply patterns and frameworks while drawing and defending conclusions to client challenges

  • Strong communication skills - able to explain complex concepts concisely and simply

  • Subject matter expertise; comfortable presenting at large and small-scale speaking engagements

  • Strong business and financial acumen

  • Deep knowledge of the global and competitive landscape within subject area as well as the interplay in that market

  • Ability to work independently, while also being intrinsically motivated to collaborate across teams and support the workflow of others, in a multicultural global team

  • Learning agile and adept with navigating highly matrixed environments

  • Ability to represent Gartner's research methodology and strategies effectively at all levels

  • Willingness and ability to travel up to 25% (where applicable)

At Gartner, Inc. (NYSE:IT), we guide the leaders who shape the world.

Our mission relies on expert analysis and bold ideas to deliver actionable, objective business and technology insights, helping enterprise leaders and their teams succeed with their mission-critical priorities.

Since our founding in 1979, we’ve grown to 20,000 associates globally who support over 13,000 client enterprises in ~90 countries and territories. What makes Gartner a great place to work?

Our vast, virtually untapped market potential offers limitless opportunities – opportunities that may not even exist right now – for you to grow professionally and flourish personally. How far you go is driven by your passion and performance.

We invest in great leaders who bring out the best in you and the company, enabling us to multiply our impact and results. This is why, year after year, we are recognized worldwide as a great place to work.

Gartner is the world authority on AI

At Gartner, you’ll join a company at the very center of the AI revolution. Gartner has proactive, objective guidance throughout clients’ AI journeys. It’s an exciting time to be at Gartner, with limitless opportunities to make a real impact, grow your skills, and build a lasting, meaningful career in a field that’s reshaping the way we operate. If you’re passionate about AI and want to be part of a team that’s guiding the leaders who shape the world, Gartner is the place for you.

In our hybrid work environment, we provide the flexibility and support for you to thrive — working virtually when it's productive to do so and getting together with colleagues in a vibrant community that is purposeful, engaging and inspiring.

Ready to grow your career with Gartner? Join us.

We’re a company on a mission - We are a unique Canadian Fintech that is the one stop shop for all financial needs of the consumer - Save, Spend, Borrow, Invest, and Protect. Changing how people make financial choices isn’t easy, though. We know that achieving our mission is full of challenges; challenges that can be complex and often unexpected, but that are always interesting, rewarding, and fun to solve as a team. This is where you come in. We are on the hunt for the right kind of people to join us and help lead us forward to continued growth.

Ratehub is looking for a Senior Product Manager to join our growing Product team. Reporting directly to the Chief Product and Technology Officer, you will own the end-to-end product strategy and execution for our Everyday Banking portfolio, partnering closely with the business unit leader to scale this high-growth segment. You’re a strategic, data-driven operator who can anticipate business needs, bring structure to ambiguous problems, and turn complex ideas into world-class digital experiences that empower millions of Canadians to make smarter financial choices.

About the Role

Wikipedia runs on curiosity — and behind the scenes, on smart financial decisions. As Senior Financial Analyst, you'll help make those decisions. Serving as the Finance Business Partner for our Communications, Marketing, and other functional teams, you'll build a deep understanding of how we invest in global brand and PR campaigns, Movement-wide communications and events, and the internal programs that keep the Foundation running well.

You'll turn financial data into insight that senior executives, managers, and program owners actually use — helping a mission-driven nonprofit spend wisely in service of something bigger than any single organization. We're looking for someone who's as energized by a hard analytical problem as they are by the mission behind it, and who does their best work in a collaborative, fast-moving environment.

This role is remote and open to candidates across UTC+2 to UTC-8 (Central European through Pacific time). Given the globally distributed nature of the team, some flexibility outside standard hours should be expected.

What You'll Do

You'll sit at the intersection of finance and mission: turning numbers into decisions that shape how Wikipedia and its sister projects grow.

  • Lead financial planning that drives mission goals. Own budgeting, forecasting, and long-term financial planning for Communications and other teams, giving leadership the clarity they need to invest in what moves the mission forward.
  • Build models that tell the real story and add value. Develop and maintain financial models that surface trends, flag risks, and reveal opportunities others might miss; the kind of analysis that changes minds in the room.
  • Turn numbers into insight and action. Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual reports, including variance analysis and KPIs that don't just document what happened, but help leaders act on what's next.
  • Bring clarity to complexity. Present financial insight and recommendations directly to leadership and stakeholders: you'll be the person who makes the numbers make sense.
  • Be a trusted partner, not just an analyst. Build deep relationships with cross-functional leaders across Communications and beyond, guiding them through planning cycles and helping them turn financial insight into smarter resourcing decisions.
  • Make the work better as you go. Spot inefficiencies and opportunities in how the Foundation plans, reports, and tracks finances, and lead the charge to build improvements.
  • Help drive strategic projects. Lend your financial lens to cross-team initiatives that shape how the Foundation operates — like building the budget model behind a global fundraising campaign, or running the financial case for launching a new approach to grant-funded community events.

What You'll Bring

You're a financial communicator as much as an analyst - someone who can turn complex data into insight that helps mission-driven leaders make better decisions, faster.

  • A Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field, plus 5+ years in financial analysis and planning; you've moved beyond the basics and are ready to shape strategy, not just report on it.
  • Direct experience budgeting, forecasting, and reporting, bonus points if it’s from a nonprofit or mission-driven environment; you understand that every dollar here maps to real-world impact.
  • Fluency in Excel/Google Sheets and modern financial modeling and data visualization tools; you build models people actually trust and use.
  • The ability to translate financial complexity into a story that resonates with non-finance stakeholders; you're as comfortable in a spreadsheet as you are in a room with executives.
  • A sharp analytical mind paired with genuine curiosity; you don't just restate the numbers, you find what they mean and why it matters.
  • Comfort operating independently in a remote, multicultural team spanning many time zones; you thrive on autonomy and know how to stay connected across distance.

Bonus points if you bring:

  • Hands-on experience with Workday Adaptive Planning
  • Experience in global nonprofit finance, grant management, or international financial operations
  • A personal connection to open-web, free knowledge communities, or the Wikimedia movement; you don't just support the mission, you believe in it

Why Join Us?

  • Your analysis will directly support Wikipedia and the other Wikimedia projects — resources that hundreds of millions of people rely on every day.
  • You'll join an inclusive, mission-first culture where finance operates as a strategic partner within the organization.
  • A genuinely remote-friendly environment spanning much of the globe, backed by benefits built for how people work today.

How to Apply

Interested candidates should submit a resume outlining their qualifications and experience. We encourage applicants from diverse backgrounds to apply.

About the Wikimedia Foundation

The Wikimedia Foundation is the nonprofit organization that operates Wikipedia and the other Wikimedia free knowledge projects. Our vision is a world in which every single human can freely share in the sum of all knowledge. We believe that everyone has the potential to contribute something to our shared knowledge, and that everyone should be able to access that knowledge freely. We host Wikipedia and the Wikimedia projects, build software experiences for reading, contributing, and sharing Wikimedia content, support the volunteer communities and partners who make Wikimedia possible, and advocate for policies that enable Wikimedia and free knowledge to thrive.

The Wikimedia Foundation is a charitable, not-for-profit organization that relies on donations. We receive donations from millions of individuals around the world, with an average donation of about $15. We also receive donations through institutional grants and gifts. The Wikimedia Foundation is a United States 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization with offices in San Francisco, California, USA.

jobs.description:
About 360 Privacy

360 Privacy is a Digital Executive Protection company that protects high-profile individuals, from the threats created by personal data exposure online.

We scan hundreds of data broker and people-search sources daily, remove client PII from the open web, and monitor the dark web and broader digital ecosystem for emerging threats. The work we do reduces the attack surface that enables social engineering, targeted harassment, doxxing, and physical targeting of the people our clients are responsible for protecting.

Our clients include Fortune 1000 companies, professional athletes, and the security teams that protect them. If you're driven by meaningful work in a fast-moving environment, we'd like to hear from you.

Role Overview

The Senior Account Manager is a high-ownership, results-driven role for someone who operates with the urgency, discretion, and expertise that our clients demand. You will manage a portfolio of C-suite executives, ultra-high-net-worth individuals, and enterprise organizations serving as their primary advisor and strategic partner on all things privacy. This is not a relationship maintenance role. We expect you to drive measurable outcomes: retention, expansion, and deep client trust built on domain expertise and proactive problem-solving. This role also requires comfort operating without an established playbook; we are a fast-moving company and the person in this seat will help define how the work gets done.

What Success Looks Like

First 90 Days

  • Full command of 360 Privacy's platform, client base, and service delivery model.
  • Deep fluency in the problem 360 Privacy exists to solve, the work the company actually delivers, and the broader ecosystem in which it operates. By the end of your first 90 days, you should be able to explain the company’s value, and the genuine complexity behind that value, to anyone you encounter in the course of your work.
  • Relationships established with every account in your portfolio; initial health assessments complete.
  • First QBRs delivered with strategic recommendations, not just status updates.

By End of Year One

  • Net Revenue Retention (NRR) at or above team target; measurable expansion across portfolio.
  • Gross Revenue Retention (GRR) reflecting strong signaling around account health and growth through proactive outreach, problem solving, and risk mitigation.
  • Clients consistently identify you as a trusted advisor integral to their privacy strategy not a vendor contact.
  • At least two accounts expanded in scope based on strategic recommendations you initiated.

Key Responsibilities

Own the Client Relationship Deeply

  • Serve as the primary advisor for a portfolio of high-profile accounts; understand their threat landscape, business objectives, and risk tolerance.
  • Build trust at the executive level; you are expected to operate comfortably with C-suite stakeholders, legal teams, and security leaders.
  • Conduct quarterly business reviews that go beyond status updates: bring strategic insight, benchmarking, and forward-looking recommendations.

Drive Retention and Growth

  • Own NRR and GRR targets for your portfolio; you understand the numbers, you own the outcomes.
  • Identify and close expansion opportunities by translating client pain points into tailored solutions across 360 Privacy's service lines.
  • Proactively surface risks before they become churn; build and execute mitigation plans without waiting to be asked.

Solve Problems with Authority

  • Navigate complex, high-stakes client situations with composure; our clients face real threats and expect expert guidance under pressure.
  • Act as a resourceful problem-solver who draws on internal teams across Sales, Product, and Support to resolve issues decisively and quickly.
  • Lead client education and adoption; ensure clients are extracting full value from the platform and understand how to leverage our capabilities.

Contribute to the Team's Playbook

  • Share field insights with internal teams to sharpen onboarding, training materials, and client-facing resources.
  • Contribute to the development of scalable account management practices as the team and client base grow.

Your Qualifications

Required

  • 5+ years in enterprise or high-touch account management, with a demonstrable record of hitting and exceeding NRR and expansion targets.
  • Direct experience managing senior stakeholders you've successfully built relationships at the C-suite or equivalent level.
  • Strong consultative instincts: you diagnose problems, recommend solutions, and lead clients to better outcomes not just relay information.
  • Analytical rigor: you track health metrics, interpret signals, and make data-backed recommendations without being told to.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication; you adjust your register for a board member, a head of security, or a legal counsel without breaking stride.
  • Comfortable operating without an established playbook: you’ve joined teams early and helped define how the work gets done.
  • Bias toward transparent, proactive communication. You flag risks early, own mistakes without deflection, and never bring a problem without a proposed path forward.

Strongly Preferred

  • Background or deep familiarity in cybersecurity, executive protection, privacy, intelligence, or a related field you can hold a substantive conversation about the threat landscape, not just the product.
  • Experience working with UHNW individuals, elite athletes, or Fortune 500 executive teams.
Salary: 125,000

The Centre for Information Resilience (CIR) is an independent organisation dedicated to exposing human rights violations, disinformation and harms against women and minorities. We achieve this through open source research, digital investigations, capacity-building with local partners, and collaboration with media to amplify our impact.

CIR was born out of a determination to expose those spreading harm – online and offline – around the world, particularly in areas of violent conflict, such as Afghanistan, Myanmar, Sudan and Ukraine. Our projects are at the forefront of efforts to investigate and document human rights abuses, war crimes, and harms against women and minorities. We work closely with multilateral and national justice accountability bodies.

About The Role

Contract Type: Contractor

Closing date: 14 August 2026 at 23:55pm

Contract length: ASAP to 31 March 2027

Hours needed for this role: 10-18 days per month , to be discussed

Location: Remote

Role’s responsibilities
The editor will be responsible for providing substantive editing and proofreading services for a range of materials including complex public reports, research documents and presentations. This role requires close collaboration with the relevant project leadership teams to ensure deadlines are met efficiently and to the highest standards. The editor will maintain the quality, consistency and accuracy of all documents, while supporting content and workflow management.

Writing and editing:

  • Provide substantive editing and proofreading for a variety of materials, including complex public reports, research documents and presentations
  • Restructure and rewrite content as necessary to improve readability
  • Ensure correct spelling, grammar and syntax, maintaining the authors' writing style

Quality assurance:

  • Maintain consistent style and format throughout documents
  • Eliminate repetition and inconsistencies
  • Ensure appropriate positioning and numbering of boxes, figures and tables
  • Ensure complete and consistent footnotes, sources and references
  • Review annexes thoroughly to highlight incomplete areas and ensure consistency
  • Prepare a complete table of contents and acronym list for each document
  • Proofread designed layout files to ensure they are print-ready

Coordination and workflow management:

  • Work with the projects' leadership team to ensure deadlines are met
  • Support content and workflow management by coordinating with investigators and team members
  • Maintain an updated database of sources, references and relevant literature
  • Ensure adherence to CIR project guidelines and standards

Requirements

Educational background:

  • Bachelor's degree. English, Journalism, Communications or a related field preferred but not essential, other specialisms will also be considered.

Professional experience:

  • Must have experience in writing, editing and proofreading complex publications and research reports
  • Experience working in a fast-paced environment
  • Proven track record of managing multiple projects simultaneously and delivering high-quality results

Technical skills:

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)
  • Familiarity with document formatting and design software (e.g., Adobe InDesign)
  • Strong understanding of style guides (e.g., AP)

Core competencies:

  • Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to quality
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Strong organisational and time-management skills
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively as part of a remote team
  • Flexibility to adapt to changing priorities and project requirements

Interpersonal skills:

  • Ability to coordinate with various stakeholders, including investigators and team members, remotely, to ensure smooth process from draft to publication
  • Strong problem-solving skills and ability to handle complex editorial task

Additional requirements

  • Ability to work under pressure and meet tight deadlines
  • Strong ethical standards and professional integrity
  • Familiarity with publication guidelines and standards programme management.

Recruitment Process

To apply, please submit your CV and complete the application form questions. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to interview, which can be conducted remotely unless specified otherwise. CIR encourages applicants from under-represented communities.

CIR is an equal opportunities employer. If you require adjustments or additional support to complete this process, please let us know in your application.

A candidate’s guide to artificial intelligence (AI) in recruitment at CIR

CIR does not use artificial intelligence (AI) or automated decision-making tools at any stage of its recruitment process. All applications are reviewed, and decisions are made, by trained members of staff.

When applying for a role, please do use AI for:

  • Check the spelling and grammar of your CV and cover letter

  • Generate mock interview questions for you to practice before your interview
  • Use AI as a support tool, not as a substitute for your own thinking or judgement

Don’t use AI to:

  • Complete any tests provided by CIR

jobs.description:
Job Title: Managing Consultant, MEQI Strategic Partnerships
Location: Remote

Description

Founded in 2004, BME Strategies is a Massachusetts-based consulting firm specializing in the design, implementation, and evaluation of public health programs for local, regional, and state government partners. Our work supports evidence-based, community-driven solutions that strengthen public health systems and advance equity across the communities we serve. At BME, our clients are on the front lines of Public Health. Priorities may shift but our commitment to supporting our partners does not. We take pride in having multi-year, multi-project engagements, often working closely as an extension of their staff. Our success comes from our shared values: a bias toward action; optimistically collaborative; willingness to navigate ambiguity; minimal ego - no job is too small or big; pursuing the equitable solution; always learning, and; committed to quality at every stage.

Position Overview

The Managing Consultant, MEQI Strategic Partnerships is a new, senior-level, dedicated business development role supporting BME's Monitoring, Evaluation and Quality Improvement (MEQI) practice, which delivers participatory local evidence, evidence at scale, continuous improvement, and data systems support to public health clients. This role will support pipeline development relevant to adjacent practice areas including clinical care access data and AI-assisted analytics. The role is managed by the MEQI Practice Area Lead, and works in close partnership with MEQI staff. Additionally, this role collaborates closely with MEQI pillar leadership and technical teams to transform client insights into well-scoped, deliverable solutions.

Because BME's growth model relies on relationship-driven trust acceleration, this position requires a dedicated business development capacity combined with a strong technical understanding. The primary market focus for this role spans public health data modernization, health information exchange (HIE), AI-assisted public health analytics, and RHTP-aligned technology and performance measurement. The right candidate brings an established network of in-state and provider health data systems and a track record of translating deep knowledge of client priorities in this space into sustained relationships and new business.

This role is an excellent fit for someone whose career has moved across public health and health IT: a former state health IT director, a health system informatics leader, a consultant who has spent years at the intersection of data modernization and public health measurement. The ideal candidate possesses the strategic instinct to rapidly analyze conferences, procurement landscapes, and partner discussions, identifying clear opportunities where BME can effectively address client needs. By cultivating deep and consistent relationships, they ensure clients have full confidence in BME long before formal opportunities arise.

Key Responsibilities

BME Org-Wide Responsibilities for Managing Consultants:

  • Managing Consultant roles at BME consist of approximately 50% project work, 20% administrative work, and 30% business development.
  • Serves as Account Manager and/or Practice Lead.
    • Contributes in a technical and advisory role
    • Offers strategic direction and quality oversight.
    • Handles relationship management and stewardship.
  • Minimal project management; instead managing accounts, staff, and practice/service areas.
  • Minimal project & account management; Minimal support of management responsibilities.
  • Supervises Associates, Senior Associates, Consultants, and Senior Consultants.
  • Manages projects to exemplary client satisfaction.
  • Recognizes business opportunities with existing clients and works with leadership to pursue.
  • Pursues and closes new business with existing clients.
  • Proactively support the outreach and sourcing of new clients.
  • Sources RFPs of interest and leads proposal development.
  • Participates in pitching of new business.

Role=Specific Responsibilities:

  • Pipeline Sourcing & Communications::
    • Maintain a consistent external presence (LinkedIn, newsletters, relevant forums) on behalf of BME relating to health data systems.
    • Coordinate with BME’s BD team, MEQI practice and firm leadership on priorities, pipeline status, and resourcing needs; own day-to-day pipeline tracking and opportunity identification across public health data modernization, AI-assisted analytics, HIE integration, and RHTP-aligned evaluation and TA.
    • Bring qualified opportunities to BD colleagues, MEQI practice and firm leadership go/no-go review and technical shaping.
    • Coordinate with BME's marketing communications function on case studies, capability briefs, and external messaging; maintain a consistent external presence on behalf of BME’s service offerings in health data systems support.
    • Other duties as assigned in support of BME's mission and growth priorities.
  • Relationship Cultivation & Partnership Development:
    • Build and maintain a network of clients, prospective primes, and partner organizations across public health data modernization, HIE, AI-assisted analytics, and RHTP-aligned technology.
    • Steward and deepen BME's existing strategic partnerships relevant to health data systems; identify and cultivate additional values-aligned partnership candidates.
    • Support teaming discussions and early-stage subcontract conversations, in coordination with MEQI practice and firm leadership.
  • Conference & Speaking Presence:
    • Identify, plan, and staff conference attendance and speaking opportunities relevant to health data systems (e.g., HIMSS, PHII Data Summit, NACCHO, ASTHO, state-level health IT forums).
    • Represent BME in venues where relationship-building and visibility are the primary goal.
    • Coordinate with MEQI practice and firm leadership to identify speaking opportunities suited to their technical expertise, and support their conference logistics.

Experience, Qualification, & Skills

  • Minimum 8 years relevant experience in business development, strategic partnership, or client relationship management in health IT, public health consulting, or a closely adjacent sector required, (10+ years preferred), including at least 4 years in a consulting firm environment
  • Minimum of 4 years people management experience, with a minimum of 3 years project management/leadership experience.
  • Master’s degree in Public Health, Epidemiology, Health Policy, Health Informatics, Biostatistics, or a closely related field required.
  • Minimum 5 years client-facing experience, including 2 or more in project leadership roles.
  • Demonstrated network in one or more of the following: state public health data modernization, health information exchange (HIE), CDC PHIG or RHTP-aligned technology, or AI-assisted analytics for health agencies.
  • Experience navigating state government procurement environments and multi-party teaming structures.
  • Track record of converting relationship presence into qualified pipeline and eventual contract awards.
  • Experience working in or alongside technical consulting teams without holding technical ownership of the work.
  • Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills; able to build credibility quickly with both public health and health IT audiences.
  • Strong written communication skills for BD materials, capability briefs, and external-facing content.
  • Disciplined pipeline management: able to qualify, prioritize, and hand off opportunities rather than accumulating volume.
  • Comfortable operating without direct authority over technical experts.
  • Familiarity with public health data systems, HIE landscapes, and federal data modernization frameworks (e.g., PHIG, TEFCA, RHTP technology requirements).
  • Working knowledge of how AI and analytics tools are being adopted in state and local public health settings.
  • Understanding of state government procurement processes and the teaming dynamics common in public health consulting.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced consulting environment.
  • Comfortable working across multiple BME teams with distinct priorities.
  • And an alignment with BME’s shared values.

Work Environment

  • This is a full-time position based in a home office environment within the U.S.
  • BME Strategies in a remote-first organization. This role may require occasional travel to client sites, conferences, or meetings as required.

Compensation & Benefits

  • BME Strategies offers a competitive compensation package that includes:
    • 6+ weeks total leave, including paid vacation, sick time, personal leave, and floating holidays;
    • Health, dental, and vision insurance, with 80% employer-paid coverage for the employee & 70% employer-paid coverage for dependents;
    • Health FSA and dependent care FSA;
    • 401(k) with employer match;
    • Employer-paid short-term and long-term disability insurance;
    • One-time technology stipend;
    • And opportunities for professional development and career growth.
  • The salary range for this position is $99,840 - $162,240 annually.

Please note: New employees are typically brought into the organization at a salary between the range minimum and the salary range midpoint, dependent upon internal equity and the budgeted amount for the position.  

How to Apply

  • To apply for this position, please complete and submit all information in the application link.
  • We expect a large volume of applicants for this position and only those candidates invited to move forward in the interview process will be contacted.
  • Important Notice on Recruitment Fraud: BME Strategies communicates with applicants only through email addresses ending @bmestrategies.com. We do not use third-party domains for recruitment outreach. If you receive communication from a different email address, please do not respond and report it to us at
  • Please note that BME Strategies is unable to sponsor work-related visas.
  • BME Strategies is made up of individuals with different strengths, experiences, and backgrounds. Diversity not only includes race and gender identity but also age, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, religion, and many other parts of one’s identity. These varied points of view are key to our success, and inclusion is everyone's responsibility. BME Strategies is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will be considered for employment without unlawful discrimination based on race, color, creed, national origin, sex, age, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, military status, prior record of arrest or conviction, or current employment status.

  • Set Schedule Days:

    • Friday: 10:00 AM – 6:00 PM EST
    • Saturday: 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM EST

  • Fifth Day (Pick One): Tuesday OR Thursday (10:00 AM – 6:00 PM)

  3. Appointment Scheduling & Management: Scheduling, confirming, and rescheduling eye care appointments while updating patient files in RevolutionEHR.

The ideal candidate is a natural relationship-builder who brings infectious positive energy to the phone, even during heavy call volumes.
